disease_name: Shrimp Black Spot / Shell Lesion Disease

pathology.target_anatomical_site: Chitinous cuticular exoskeleton (carapace, abdominal terga, pleura, uropods, telson)
pathology.etiology: Chitinolytic bacteria (Vibrio harveyi, Vibrio parahaemolyticus, Aeromonas spp., Pseudomonas spp.) producing extracellular chitinases that enzymatically degrade the chitin-protein matrix of the shell
pathology.host_response: Shrimp prophenoloxidase (proPO) activation causing cellular melanization, resulting in characteristic brownish-black necrotic pockmarks, eroded lesions, and cuticular ulcers
pathology.environmental_triggers: High organic sediment, low dissolved oxygen (< 4.5 mg/L), excessive stocking density, physical shell abrasions

scientific_distinction_from_black_gill.black_gill_site: Branchial lamellae (gills beneath branchiostegite lateral margin)
scientific_distinction_from_black_gill.black_gill_etiology: Fusarium solani (fungal), Zoothamnium/Epistylis ciliates, or suspended colloidal silt fouling
scientific_distinction_from_black_gill.relabeling_restriction: Strictly prohibited: Public datasets containing Black Gill (such as Mendeley ShrimpDiseaseImageBD or bd-fish-disease-dataset) cannot be relabeled as Black Spot without invalidating pathological integrity

verified_dataset_status.literature_source: Minh-Huy Bui et al., 'A Novel Farm-Level Dataset and Real-Time Detection Framework for Shrimp Black Spot Disease', IEEE ICCITX 2026
verified_dataset_status.public_direct_download_mirror: Not yet released under open-access mirror as of 2026 conference proceedings (available via author request)
